articles.title: [GNR A0 PO][X1][X3][RAS_DM] [2S] UPI CRC error is not reported at OS if previous error happens in a different port
articles.description: Very few errors are reported at OS level after performing CRC injections randomizing the UPI ports 2022.12 telemetry: unique entry = a91c9e287d0711edb31fa4bf018cc9a2 [01:16:16.777] I: fisher: stats: PASS = 9 - FAIL = 11 After some experiments was found that: 1. Errors are reported if are injected back to back in the same port 2. When a second error is injected in a different port the error is logged in kti_mc_st but not at OS level.
comments: Hi Diego, Does this TC passed with 1S? A 2S issue reported from silicon. Maybe it's worth having a try with PYSV workaround.  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- From: Fausto, Matthew B Sent: Tuesday, December 20, 2022 2:06 PM To: GNR VST Cc: Fausto, Matthew B Subject: GNR Val: To all teams doing 2Skt debug - upi routing table issue - PYSV code being verified then to be cloned to BIOS Feature   If you are involved in any 2Skt execution, please note this sighting and the UPI Routing Table updates.  Once enough cycles to verify it is good, this will be root-caused to a BIOS Feature for implementation.   So if you are doing 2Skt debug, please try these PYSV settings.     [GNR A0 PO][X1][2S] Seeing Core Data Error on 2 socket platform for DWr thread with D2K enabled https://hsdes.intel.com/appstore/article/#/16018792887/main

Hi @Wanyan, Feiting this scenario is not applicable for 1S platforms as is injection in the UPI link, so first steps will be to see if the problem with the injection is coming from an specific UPI port or injector response. Worth to mention that logic is ported from EGS where injection flow used to work all the time
Oh, it's UPI, my fault. Let's start from error log analysis. Thanks Diego!
@Garcia Rodriguez, Diego what's the latest status of this TC?
Low injection rate is worst in X3. telemetry: entry = 2023.02/e43a41dfa5ce11ed87ca0242ac110002 Will collect the injector parameters in order to look for a pattern in failing and  passing cases.

With current data, it seems this is unique to X1/X3. Running on 2S X2 with current UPI topology this issue is NOT shown.  Currently running (still in progress) : telemetry: entry = 2023.02/447d87a8a74f11ed90a80007e9342bdf [root@gnr-bkc UPI_CRC_Injection]# dmidecode | grep BHS         Version: BHSDCRB1.SYS.0020.D30.2301201241 As of now: 24 successful cycles UPI topology is:  import graniterapids.upi.upiStatus as upis upis.printTopology -------> upis.printTopology() 2S4Q Topology S0_P0 S1_P1 S0_P1 S1_P0 S0_P2 S1_P2 S0_P3 S1_P3 S1_P0 S0_P1 S1_P1 S0_P0 S1_P2 S0_P2 S1_P3 S0_P3 -------------       ------------- |          3*********3          | |          2*********2          | |     0     |       |     1     | |          1*********0          | |          0*********1          | -------------       -------------

I have been performing several experiments to try to isolate the failure. This experiments has happened in a X1 and X3 system in parallel: [1] Injecting in upi port 0 (socket0, io0) and fixed parameters in einjretryactivemode and einjnumretry - PASS [2] Injecting in upi port 0 (socket0, io0) and randomizing einjretryactivemode - PASS [3] Injecting in upi port 0 (socket0, io0) and randomizing einjretryactivemode and einjnumretry- PASS [4] Injecting in upi port 5 (socket0, io1) and randomizing einjretryactivemode and einjnumretry-FAIL [5]Injecting in upi port 2 (socket0, io1) and randomizing einjretryactivemode and einjnumretry-FAIL At this point we can confirm that the injector parameters are correct and the suspicion was that the ports in io1 were the ones presenting the issue but after injecting back to port0 the errors are not been seen at OS level. Looking at the injector it shows that the error was injected: In [22]: sv.sockets.ios.uncore.upi.upis.upi_regs.ktirxeinjctl0.errinjst Out[22]: socket0.io0.uncore.upi.upi0.upi_regs.ktirxeinjctl0.errinjst - 0x00000001 socket0.io0.uncore.upi.upi1.upi_regs.ktirxeinjctl0.errinjst - 0x00000000 socket0.io1.uncore.upi.upi2.upi_regs.ktirxeinjctl0.errinjst - 0x00000000 socket0.io1.uncore.upi.upi3.upi_regs.ktirxeinjctl0.errinjst - 0x00000000 socket0.io1.uncore.upi.upi4.upi_regs.ktirxeinjctl0.errinjst - 0x00000000 socket0.io1.uncore.upi.upi5.upi_regs.ktirxeinjctl0.errinjst - 0x00000000 socket1.io0.uncore.upi.upi0.upi_regs.ktirxeinjctl0.errinjst - 0x00000000 socket1.io0.uncore.upi.upi1.upi_regs.ktirxeinjctl0.errinjst - 0x00000000 socket1.io1.uncore.upi.upi2.upi_regs.ktirxeinjctl0.errinjst - 0x00000000 socket1.io1.uncore.upi.upi3.upi_regs.ktirxeinjctl0.errinjst - 0x00000000 socket1.io1.uncore.upi.upi4.upi_regs.ktirxeinjctl0.errinjst - 0x00000000 socket1.io1.uncore.upi.upi5.upi_regs.ktirxeinjctl0.errinjst - 0x00000000 Also I do see that upi mca has logged the errors in the ports where the errors were not seen at OS level. In [23]: sv.sockets.ios.uncore.upi.upis.upi_regs.kti_mc_st Out[23]: socket0.io0.uncore.upi.upi0.upi_regs.kti_mc_st - 0x8800034000300e0f socket0.io0.uncore.upi.upi1.upi_regs.kti_mc_st - 0x8800014000300e0f socket0.io1.uncore.upi.upi2.upi_regs.kti_mc_st - 0x8800010000300e0f socket0.io1.uncore.upi.upi3.upi_regs.kti_mc_st - 0x0000000000000000 socket0.io1.uncore.upi.upi4.upi_regs.kti_mc_st - 0x0000000000000000 socket0.io1.uncore.upi.upi5.upi_regs.kti_mc_st - 0x8800010000300e0f socket1.io0.uncore.upi.upi0.upi_regs.kti_mc_st - 0x0000000000000000 socket1.io0.uncore.upi.upi1.upi_regs.kti_mc_st - 0x0000000000000000 socket1.io1.uncore.upi.upi2.upi_regs.kti_mc_st - 0x0000000000000000 socket1.io1.uncore.upi.upi3.upi_regs.kti_mc_st - 0x0000000000000000 socket1.io1.uncore.upi.upi4.upi_regs.kti_mc_st - 0x0000000000000000 socket1.io1.uncore.upi.upi5.upi_regs.kti_mc_st - 0x0000000000000000 Could it be an override rules problem? TITLE: [GNR A0 PO][X1][X3][RAS_DM] [2S] UPI CRC error is not reported at OS if previous error happens in a different port

DESCRIPTION:
Very few errors are reported at OS level after performing CRC injections randomizing the UPI ports 2022.12 telemetry: unique entry = a91c9e287d0711edb31fa4bf018cc9a2 [01:16:16.777] I: fisher: stats: PASS = 9 - FAIL = 11 After some experiments was found that: 1. Errors are reported if are injected back to back in the same port 2. When a second error is injected in a different port the error is logged in kti_mc_st but not at OS level.

COMMENTS:
Hi Diego, Does this TC passed with 1S? A 2S issue reported from silicon. Maybe it's worth having a try with PYSV workaround.  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- From: Fausto, Matthew B Sent: Tuesday, December 20, 2022 2:06 PM To: GNR VST Cc: Fausto, Matthew B Subject: GNR Val: To all teams doing 2Skt debug - upi routing table issue - PYSV code being verified then to be cloned to BIOS Feature   If you are involved in any 2Skt execution, please note this sighting and the UPI Routing Table updates.  Once enough cycles to verify it is good, this will be root-caused to a BIOS Feature for implementation.   So if you are doing 2Skt debug, please try these PYSV settings.     [GNR A0 PO][X1][2S] Seeing Core Data Error on 2 socket platform for DWr thread with D2K enabled https://hsdes.intel.com/appstore/article/#/16018792887/main
Hi @Wanyan, Feiting this scenario is not applicable for 1S platforms as is injection in the UPI link, so first steps will be to see if the problem with the injection is coming from an specific UPI port or injector response. Worth to mention that logic is ported from EGS where injection flow used to work all the time
Oh, it's UPI, my fault. Let's start from error log analysis. Thanks Diego!
@Garcia Rodriguez, Diego what's the latest status of this TC?
Low injection rate is worst in X3. telemetry: entry = 2023.02/e43a41dfa5ce11ed87ca0242ac110002 Will collect the injector parameters in order to look for a pattern in failing and  passing cases.
With current data, it seems this is unique to X1/X3. Running on 2S X2 with current UPI topology this issue is NOT shown.  Currently running (still in progress) : telemetry: entry = 2023.02/447d87a8a74f11ed90a80007e9342bdf [root@gnr-bkc UPI_CRC_Injection]# dmidecode | grep BHS         Version: BHSDCRB1.SYS.0020.D30.2301201241 As of now: 24 successful cycles UPI topology is:  import graniterapids.upi.upiStatus as upis upis.printTopology -------> upis.printTopology() 2S4Q Topology S0_P0 S1_P1 S0_P1 S1_P0 S0_P2 S1_P2 S0_P3 S1_P3 S1_P0 S0_P1 S1_P1 S0_P0 S1_P2 S0_P2 S1_P3 S0_P3 -------------       ------------- |          3*********3          | |          2*********2          | |     0     |       |     1     | |          1*********0          | |          0*********1          | -------------       -------------
I have been performing several experiments to try to isolate the failure. This experiments has happened in a X1 and X3 system in parallel: [1] Injecting in upi port 0 (socket0, io0) and fixed parameters in einjretryactivemode and einjnumretry - PASS [2] Injecting in upi port 0 (socket0, io0) and randomizing einjretryactivemode - PASS [3] Injecting in upi port 0 (socket0, io0) and randomizing einjretryactivemode and einjnumretry- PASS [4] Injecting in upi port 5 (socket0, io1) and randomizing einjretryactivemode and einjnumretry-FAIL [5]Injecting in upi port 2 (socket0, io1) and randomizing einjretryactivemode and einjnumretry-FAIL At this point we can confirm that the injector parameters are correct and the suspicion was that the ports in io1 were the ones presenting the issue but after injecting back to port0 the errors are not been seen at OS level. Looking at the injector it shows that the error was injected: In [22]: sv.sockets.ios.uncore.upi.upis.upi_regs.ktirxeinjctl0.errinjst Out[22]: socket0.io0.uncore.upi.upi0.upi_regs.ktirxeinjctl0.errinjst - 0x00000001 socket0.io0.uncore.upi.upi1.upi_regs.ktirxeinjctl0.errinjst - 0x00000000 socket0.io1.uncore.upi.upi2.upi_regs.ktirxeinjctl0.errinjst - 0x00000000 socket0.io1.uncore.upi.upi3.upi_regs.ktirxeinjctl0.errinjst - 0x00000000 socket0.io1.uncore.upi.upi4.upi_regs.ktirxeinjctl0.errinjst - 0x00000000 socket0.io1.uncore.upi.upi5.upi_regs.ktirxeinjctl0.errinjst - 0x00000000 socket1.io0.uncore.upi.upi0.upi_regs.ktirxeinjctl0.errinjst - 0x00000000 socket1.io0.uncore.upi.upi1.upi_regs.ktirxeinjctl0.errinjst - 0x00000000 socket1.io1.uncore.upi.upi2.upi_regs.ktirxeinjctl0.errinjst - 0x00000000 socket1.io1.uncore.upi.upi3.upi_regs.ktirxeinjctl0.errinjst - 0x00000000 socket1.io1.uncore.upi.upi4.upi_regs.ktirxeinjctl0.errinjst - 0x00000000 socket1.io1.uncore.upi.upi5.upi_regs.ktirxeinjctl0.errinjst - 0x00000000 Also I do see that upi mca has logged the errors in the ports where the errors were not seen at OS level. Raising HSD severity.
I found a pattern in this failure: All the ports has been injected the error successfully In [42]: sv.sockets.ios.uncore.upi.upis.upi_regs.ktirxeinjctl0.errinjst Out[42]: socket0.io0.uncore.upi.upi0.upi_regs.ktirxeinjctl0.errinjst - 0x00000001 2nd injected port  socket0.io0.uncore.upi.upi1.upi_regs.ktirxeinjctl0.errinjst - 0x00000001 1st injected port socket0.io1.uncore.upi.upi2.upi_regs.ktirxeinjctl0.errinjst - 0x00000000 socket0.io1.uncore.upi.upi3.upi_regs.ktirxeinjctl0.errinjst - TITLE: [GNR A1][RAS_DM] CsmiDynamicDisable is incorrectly enabled by default by BIOS

DESCRIPTION:
It was agreed for Servers back in 2021 during RAS WG that the default for CsmiDynamicDisable should be set to disabled for SPR and beyond (while a UBOX thresholding scheme is decided that doesn't disable SMI's forever). But we should not be masking of CSMI's forever per MCi_BANK. Current BHS BIOS builds are not honoring that func_requirement here https://hsdes.intel.com/appstore/article/#/16013180336 and breaks the agreement since BHS and next-gens were also marked as affected. articles.title: [GNR] Bios option to set uncore freq Range update needed from "8 to 2.2" (all of uncore) to 8 to 22 for Uncore Compute and 8-2.5(or 2.4 based on SKU fused max) for Uncore IO
articles.description: On GNR/SRF, the uncore has the compute and IO parts. Bios needs to list both "Uncore Compute" and "Uncore IO" freq ranges . Currently, there is only one "uncore freq" option in the Bios that sets all uncore compute and uncore IOs to the same freq and in the range of 8 to 22 (0.8 GHz to 2.2 GHz) This works for the "Uncore Compute" since the spec range is 8 - 22. However, it limits the "Uncore IO" to 22 while it can go up to 25 based on the SKU. In some SKUs it can only go up to 24. Settings in the Bios: Socket Configuration-->Advanced Power Management Configuration-->CPU - Advanced PM Tuning --> Uncore Freq Control -->Current Uncore Ratio Range --> Proposed Solution: 1. In place of "Current Uncore Ratio Range 08 - 22 Add "Current Uncore Compute Ratio Range 08 -- 22" and "Current Uncore IO Ratio Range 08 -- 24" or "Current Uncore IO Ratio Range 08 -- 25" depending on the fused max Uncore IO freq. Also make sure that the min is 08 or 04. Per the meeting 8/6/2024, we have two options, Bios to decide on one and take it to the next GK meeting Option#1: Update the ranges in the Bios to add compute 8 -22 for uncore-compute and 4-25 for uncore-IO Option#2: Do a complete breakdown at SKT level into individual IO can compute dies like below 2S example: SKT0 à à Compute DIE0 à 08-22 à Compute DIE1 à 08-22 à Compute DIE2 à 08-22 à IO Die0 à 04-25 or 04-24 à IO Die1 à 04-25 or 04-24 SKT1 à à Compute DIE0 à 08-22 à Compute DIE1 à 08-22 à Compute DIE2 à 08-22 à IO Die0 à 04-25 or 04-24 à IO Die1 à 04-25 or 04-24 AR: Bios team (Yun and Robin) will decide it implementation of either Option#1 or Option#2.

(intel.com)  if it is a new request, it should be a feature request, not bug.

It is expected behavior. The displayed range is aggregated min/max as common range for both Compute die and IO die. BIOS Output Display BIOS to read the SST_PP_INFO-11 register in the SST HAS for each fabric in the die and SST-PP level and display the aggregated min/max for the package for the choose SST-PP level, as described below. BIOS will know the min and P0 bounds for each dielet fabric frequency using the CFC_MIN_RATIO and CFC_P0_RATIO fuses or the SST TPMI register filed for min and max frequency for a dielet. The customer supported frequency bound will be as follows: Min frequency bound Limit = max(minimum supported frequency on dielets). For example, in GNR this is max(400 MHz, 800 MHz) = 800 MHz Max frequency bound Limit = min(maximum supported frequency on dielets). For example, we could have a scenario where GNR max limit will be min(2500, 2800) = 2500. The above restrictions on min and max resolutions are only relevant when customer changes the frequency using BIOS. Customers are free to change per die fabric frequency using TPMI driver from some other software, such as OS. https://docs.intel.com/documents/pm_doc/src/server/GNR/Features/Hierarchical%20UFS/HPM_UFS.html#bios-output-display
it is by design so customer usage manual should be well descripted here or some document?

TITLE: [GNR] Bios option to set uncore freq Range update needed from "8 to 2.2" (all of uncore) to 8 to 22 for Uncore Compute and 8-2.5(or 2.4 based on SKU fused max) for Uncore IO

DESCRIPTION:
On GNR/SRF, the uncore has the compute and IO parts. Bios needs to list both "Uncore Compute" and "Uncore IO" freq ranges . Currently, there is only one "uncore freq" option in the Bios that sets all uncore compute and uncore IOs to the same freq and in the range of 8 to 22 (0.8 GHz to 2.2 GHz) This works for the "Uncore Compute" since the spec range is 8 - 22. However, it limits the "Uncore IO" to 22 while it can go up to 25 based on the SKU. In some SKUs it can only go up to 24. Settings in the Bios: Socket Configuration-->Advanced Power Management Configuration-->CPU - Advanced PM Tuning --> Uncore Freq Control -->Current Uncore Ratio Range --> Proposed Solution: 1. In place of "Current Uncore Ratio Range 08 - 22 Add "Current Uncore Compute Ratio Range 08 -- 22" and "Current Uncore IO Ratio Range 08 -- 24" or "Current Uncore IO Ratio Range 08 -- 25" depending on the fused max Uncore IO freq. Also make sure that the min is 08 or 04. Per the meeting 8/6/2024, we have two options, Bios to decide on one and take it to the next GK meeting Option#1: Update the ranges in the Bios to add compute 8 -22 for uncore-compute and 4-25 for uncore-IO Option#2: Do a complete breakdown at SKT level into individual IO can compute dies like below 2S example: SKT0 à à Compute DIE0 à 08-22 à Compute DIE1 à 08-22 à Compute DIE2 à 08-22 à IO Die0 à 04-25 or 04-24 à IO Die1 à 04-25 or 04-24 SKT1 à à Compute DIE0 à 08-22 à Compute DIE1 à 08-22 à Compute DIE2 à 08-22 à IO Die0 à 04-25 or 04-24 à IO Die1 à 04-25 or 04-24 AR: Bios team (Yun and Robin) will decide it implementation of either Option#1 or Option#2.

COMMENTS:

Is this expected_behavior? Hi @Keesara, Sreekanth R - What is the functional impact due to this observation? BIOS menu & knobs haven't changed for quite some time. And, SRF-SP has already declared PV. Any reason, why this issue is surfacing now? For now, let us track this sighting as a exposure/priority 2-high as data is insufficient to call this as a showstopper. thank you Shashi Kiran [SRF Platform Sysdebug Lead]
@Zeng, Star the uncore frequency ratio options is 8-22 should be aligned with SPEC. right ? we have a clarified on a similar PAE sighting 15016397755 - [PNP][GNR-AP][SRF-SP][CRB][Perf] IO die uncore frequency could not keep at max when setting uncore frequency ratio to max in BIOS. (intel.com)  if it is a new request, it should be a feature request, not bug.
It is expected behavior. The displayed range is aggregated min/max as common range for both Compute die and IO die. BIOS Output Display BIOS to read the SST_PP_INFO-11 register in the SST HAS for each fabric in the die and SST-PP level and display the aggregated min/max for the package for the choose SST-PP level, as described below. BIOS will know the min and P0 bounds for each dielet fabric frequency using the CFC_MIN_RATIO and CFC_P0_RATIO fuses or the SST TPMI register filed for min and max frequency for a dielet. The customer supported frequency bound will be as follows: Min frequency bound Limit = max(minimum supported frequency on dielets). For example, in GNR this is max(400 MHz, 800 MHz) = 800 MHz Max frequency bound Limit = min(maximum supported frequency on dielets). For example, we could have a scenario where GNR max limit will be min(2500, 2800) = 2500. The above restrictions on min and max resolutions are only relevant when customer changes the frequency using BIOS. Customers are free to change per die fabric frequency using TPMI driver from some other software, such as OS. https://docs.intel.com/documents/pm_doc/src/server/GNR/Features/Hierarchical%20UFS/HPM_UFS.html#bios-output-display
it is by design so customer usage manual should be well descripted here or some document?

Actually, per previous talk with original HAS owner, it was intended to have simple BIOS implementation for simple usage, that is why "The UFS advanced control is not needed in BIOS." was highlighted in https://docs.intel.com/documents/pm_doc/src/server/GNR/Features/Hierarchical%20UFS/HPM_UFS.html#bios-interface. Impact: BIOS show "Current Uncore Ratio Range" is 8-2.2 for "Uncore-computer" and "Uncore-IO", but "Uncore-IO" can go up to 25.

articles.title: [CWF-AP A0 PO] [First_Boot][ICCCI] Boot to CentOS and keeping system idle for few minutes resulting in GPSB Timeout
articles.description: Ingredients: PO IFWI: \\scsfls0001.amr.corp.intel.com\CWF\PO_IFWI\ICCCI_IC_Merged_IFWI\WW36.3 Recipe: 144 Core and 48 LLC Steps to Reproduce: Note: Used pre-flashed IFWI as used by Mesh Team (SNC Bios Knob was probably enabled) 1. Boot to CentOS 2. Run lspci command in OS and sls command in PythonSV 3. Within few minutes --> Caterr is observed (MCA_GPSB_TO) For Recovery: 1. Re-Flash BIOS 2. Restart PythonSV and Run Bootscript 3. Boot to CentOS 4. Issue was not observed. (Waited for 5 mins in idle state, later ran lspci command and waited for 3 mins, even running PythonSV commands did not cause any hang) MCA Dump Log Attached: MCA_Dump.log
comments: As a part of the WA for  14020741582 , prime code   does a RMW operation to an ADL register  (REG_OFFSET_RTB4_ACTION_OUT_2) in scf_b2hot instances  every 1ms . The read to the  REG_OFFSET_RTB4_ACTION_OUT_2 is taking longer than 1ms  triggering the  MCA_GPSB_TIMEOUT . NOTE : The register read does finish up successfully . NEXT STEP : Please increase the gpsb timeout  by modifying the  gpsb_mca_timeout_val_us pcudata  variable to  0x5dc ( 1.5 millisecond ) from the default setting of  0x3e8  (1 millisecond) to see if the failure recreates

if the failure is consistently recreated , Please try disabling the WA using the below pcudata overrrides  sv.socket0.ios.pcudata.hsd_14020741591_workaround_enable = 0 sv.socket0.ios.pcudata.hsd_14020741582_workaround_enable = 0

On GPSB TO re-creation. On next boot, the below work around was applied and stressed the system the system for 15 minutes with LSPCI -VVV command. The system did not generate the GPSB TO . Further steps to try for More hrs to stress to check is below WA disable removes the GPSB time out

We need to try one more experiment --- Can we disable only one workaround that has the 1ms periodic piece? hsd_14020741582_workaround_enable = false These two are different bugs: Bug1 (Reset): https://sdg74-web.sc.intel.com/pcode/w4/master/_h_s_d_14020741591.html  Bug2 (Reset + Runtime) : https://sdg74-web.sc.intel.com/pcode/w4/master/_h_s_d_14020741582.html -------------------------------notes -------------------------------------- From the side email thread - here is the analysis done to review the GNR/SRF HSD and I think the notes here might be useful as documentation. -------------------------------------------------------------------------- Checking on this WA status in CWF https://hsdes.intel.com/appstore/article/#/14022320913 [SysDebug FWD][GNR][SRF][AI-RDOP] ras-unified workloads combo hits TOR TO - Bank 7: be000000000c110a - slowness = AI-RDOP / B2HOT ADL W/A interactions     Here is what happened in chronological order.   AI-RDOP feature added This was added for all GNR portfolio.  Basically it was doing auto idle programming into the RC registers for PC55. ADL SCF Col W/A added  -- this workaround had two pieces – Reset/runtime.  The runtime piece was running periodically every 1ms (slowloop) and doing RMW of certain registers. GNR HSD - https://hsdes.intel.com/appstore/article/#/14020741591 FAS - https://sdg74-web.sc.intel.com/pcode/w4/master/_h_s_d_14020741591.html AI-RDOP x ADL B2Hot W/a added -- to prevent adl wakeup to gain back power savings GNR HSD - https://hsdes.intel.com/appstore/article/#/14021394400 AI-RDOP Disabled by default on SRF AI-RDOP Tuning + ADL B2HOT w/a removed -- as it was causing TOR TOs   The CWF code is similar to GNR at this point.  SRF has the entire feature disabled.   If you want to disable #2 above, I suggested Vivek to set the following before phase5 reset (put a breakpoint) hsd_14020741591_workaround_enable = false      ---   reset piece of the WA  -- one time programming. hsd_14020741582_workaround_enable = false      ---   It has both reset and runtime pieces.  I see that some values are similar and some are different. Checking with GNR team. This will basically get the periodic 1ms programming out of the way.
dumps at \\scsfls0001.amr.corp.intel.com\CWF\Users\vseethar\gpsb_to

with the  patch \\scsfls0001.amr.corp.intel.com\CWF\Users\PrimeCode\debug_patches\F0580139 . Seeing system soft hang  . The SUT console is unresponsive with no MCA  \\amr.corp.intel.com\ec\proj\debug\CWF\Users\vseethar\softhang.log Need to enable TOR dump scripts  to dump TOR content  NEXT STEP : Trying overriding the  partial WA via pythonsv  to see if that also sees the same issue and debug from there

able to recreate the failure  with F0580157  file://SCCV69A-CIFS.sc.intel.com/dcsg_0729/users/vdc/CWF/prod/F0580157  \\scsfls0001.amr.corp.intel.com\CWF\Users\PrimeCode\debug_patches\F0580157  1f0  https://hsdes.intel.com/appstore/article/#/14023430059  182 _wa enabled  + iosf histo enabled  /nfs/site/disks/dcsg_0729/users/lbhat/histo_patch_v2    Set IosfHistoBuffer::iosf_histo_buff_allow_store_on_err = true  \\scsfls0001.amr.corp.intel.com\CWF\Users\PrimeCode\debug_patches\F058015B    Steps to recreate : Boot the system  unlock the system  execute sv.refresh() should see the GPSB TO happen  The TIMEOUT is  always to portid 0x2b0  ( This is the portid targeted by  182 wa , every 1 ms a  read write write sequence is done ) Looking into the  socket discovery code .  ( step 3).  The failure is isolated to the add_fuse step in io0 component     def find_all(self):         """         Discover all devices and load the correct PythonSv component.         This function will include common code across all access mechanisms. Any function that is repeated in all base accesses needs to be added here.         Returns:             Sockets: The iterator object which contains any numbers of sockets that were created.         """         self.reset_stepping()         self.example_gnr()         self.example_gnrd()         self.example_srf()         self.reset_matrixes()         self.add_pysv_config()         self._early_break = False         sockets = self._find_all_from_base()         if self._pysv_access == "redfish":             return sockets         if sockets is None:             return []         elif len(sockets) == 0:             return []         self.add_taps_path(sockets)         self.add_mc_type(sockets)         self.add_xtor_name(sockets)         self.add_soc_tap2sbname(sockets)         self.add_ibl_component(sockets)         self.add_fuse(sockets)         self.get_chop(sockets)         self.add_pcudata(sockets)         self.add_pcodeio_map_component(sockets)         self.add_helpers(sockets)         self.add_cabist(sockets)         self.add_ijtag(sockets)

updates : [Andrade Aparicio, Johel] Okay so yeah its basically that "fuse_controller_revision"  function. For some reason that function is triggering the erorr. For now he only provided the WA for that:    from svtools.chassis_fuse import settings settings.DISABLE_FUSE_CTL_VERSION_CHECK = True Ok so quick update. I was able to confirm that the function in the discovery is the one that is making this to fail.  I'm already seeing this with Parra Gonzalez, Luis Alfonso to determine what could be the issue.    To be more specific is this function in the fuse_tool (chassis_fuse):
updates [ suchitra ] 1. The GPSB TO does not happen when  SNC_EN bios knob is turned off
The endpoint timing out at pcode : IODIE adl.0.scf_b2hot.0 688 0 2B0 IODIE adl.0.scf_b2hot.8 688 4 2B0

Per the request forwarded to 16025640654, PrimeCode removed the WA, but sounds like that was temporary for the customer PO, so this ticket still needs work to be root caused and the workaround should be put back. So FYI if somebody expects this workaround, it won't be in new PrimeCode builds (anything after nightly-primecode-2024ww40-2785.tar.gz will not have the WA).

This is tracked in sighting central https://hsdes.intel.com/appstore/article/#/14023862246., W/A is available to unblock the issue as https://hsdes.intel.com/appstore/article/#/1666271820. from svtools.chassis_fuse import settings settings.DISABLE_FUSE_CTL_VERSION_CHECK = True

TITLE: [CWF-AP A0 PO] [First_Boot][ICCCI] Boot to CentOS and keeping system idle for few minutes resulting in GPSB Timeout

DESCRIPTION:
Ingredients: PO IFWI: \\scsfls0001.amr.corp.intel.com\CWF\PO_IFWI\ICCCI_IC_Merged_IFWI\WW36.3 Recipe: 144 Core and 48 LLC Steps to Reproduce: Note: Used pre-flashed IFWI as used by Mesh Team (SNC Bios Knob was probably enabled) 1. Boot to CentOS 2. Run lspci command in OS and sls command in PythonSV 3. Within few minutes --> Caterr is observed (MCA_GPSB_TO) For Recovery: 1. Re-Flash BIOS 2. Restart PythonSV and Run Bootscript 3. Boot to CentOS 4. Issue was not observed. (Waited for 5 mins in idle state, later ran lspci command and waited for 3 mins, even running PythonSV commands did not cause any hang) MCA Dump Log Attached: MCA_Dump.log

COMMENTS:
As a part of the WA for  14020741582 , prime code   does a RMW operation to an ADL register  (REG_OFFSET_RTB4_ACTION_OUT_2) in scf_b2hot instances  every 1ms . The read to the  REG_OFFSET_RTB4_ACTION_OUT_2 is taking longer than 1ms  triggering the  MCA_GPSB_TIMEOUT . NOTE : The register read does finish up successfully . NEXT STEP : Please increase the gpsb timeout  by modifying the  gpsb_mca_timeout_val_us pcudata  variable to  0x5dc ( 1.5 millisecond ) from the default setting of  0x3e8  (1 millisecond) to see if the failure recreates
if the failure is consistently recreated , Please try disabling the WA using the below pcudata overrrides  sv.socket0.ios.pcudata.hsd_14020741591_workaround_enable = 0 sv.socket0.ios.pcudata.hsd_14020741582_workaround_enable = 0
On GPSB TO re-creation. On next boot, the below work around was applied and stressed the system the system for 15 minutes with LSPCI -VVV command. The system did not generate the GPSB TO . Further steps to try for More hrs to stress to check is below WA disable removes the GPSB time out
We need to try one more experiment --- Can we disable only one workaround that has the 1ms periodic piece? hsd_14020741582_workaround_enable = false These two are different bugs: Bug1 (Reset): https://sdg74-web.sc.intel.com/pcode/w4/master/_h_s_d_14020741591.html  Bug2 (Reset + Runtime) : https://sdg74-web.sc.intel.com/pcode/w4/master/_h_s_d_14020741582.html -------------------------------notes -------------------------------------- From the side email thread - here is the analysis done to review the GNR/SRF HSD and I think the notes here might be useful as documentation. -------------------------------------------------------------------------- Checking on this WA status in CWF https://hsdes.intel.com/appstore/article/#/14022320913 [SysDebug FWD][GNR][SRF][AI-RDOP] ras-unified workloads combo hits TOR TO - Bank 7: be000000000c110a - slowness = AI-RDOP / B2HOT ADL W/A interactions     Here is what happened in chronological order.   AI-RDOP feature added This was added for all GNR portfolio.  Basically it was doing auto idle programming into the RC registers for PC55. ADL SCF Col W/A added  -- this workaround had two pieces – Reset/runtime.  The runtime piece was running periodically every 1ms (slowloop) and doing RMW of certain registers. GNR HSD - https://hsdes.intel.com/appstore/article/#/14020741591 FAS - https://sdg74-web.sc.intel.com/pcode/w4/master/_h_s_d_14020741591.html AI-RDOP x ADL B2Hot W/a added -- to prevent adl wakeup to gain back power savings GNR HSD - https://hsdes.intel.com/appstore/article/#/14021394400 AI-RDOP Disabled by default on SRF AI-RDOP Tuning + ADL B2HOT w/a removed -- as it was causing TOR TOs   The CWF code is similar to GNR at this point.  SRF has the entire feature disabled.   If you want to disable #2 above, I suggested Vivek to set the following before phase5 reset (put a breakpoint) hsd_14020741591_workaround_enable = false      ---   reset piece of the WA  -- one time programming. hsd_14020741582_workaround_enable = false      ---   It has both reset and runtime pieces.  I see that some values are similar and some are different. Checking with GNR team. This will basically get the periodic 1ms programming out of the way.

comments: Appears this may be a MCHECK error due to the population of the DIMMs on the platform. Please ensure the platform has the DIMMs populated in a configuration supporting SGX and TDX - requires uniform population across slots.

Issue reproducible on IFWI : BHSDCRB1.86B.3698.D03.2411041040 (WW45.1 PO purple release) We are hitting an UC MCA error while trying to start the sgx.aesm service on centos  #systemctl start sgx.aesm.services ************************************************************** System 1 : SC09WVAW7493.amr.corp.intel.com Board : Avenue City Stepping : 1S A0 Fuse : Q5VJ (fused) Bios ID         : BHSDCRB1.86B.3698.D03.2411041040 Kernel : 6.8.0-cwf.bkc.6.8.8.2.9.x86_64DIMM Config : 1DPC Micron RA64GB(16Gbx4DR)7200Freq  SGX DCAP      : SGX-2.24.100.3-v1-centos9 @Bombien, Derek  Platform is having 1DPC Micron RA64GB DIMMs, there is no MCHCEK error we could find on this failure. Hangdumps Core and Uncore MCA dumps Status scope attached to Axon page
@Colton, Alexis A Could you please have a check on this UBOX and PUNIT MCA error found during sgx aesm service activation in CentOS 6.8 kernel

ISCLK errors are usually occurring only during reset. Was an error generated that sent you back through another reset? Also have we confirmed we have the SRF/GNR patch that deals with SGX keys on warm reset due to the IO die bug (that also impacts KPT keys)?
@Cummins, Michael K  We see system hungs ASAP we try to start the SGX aesm services at CentOS,(systemctl start sgx.aesm.serives). Can you point us what SRF/GNR SGX key issue you talking about.

Have you already addressed the other CWF SGX sighting: https://hsdes.intel.com/appstore/article/#/14023936962 The SRF/GNR issue that impacted SGX and KPT is from here: https://hsdes.intel.com/appstore/article/#/15013577215 The summary of the issue is that SGX and KPT keys were listed as pull once for IO0. However there is a power down that occurs after the initial fuse pull for QAT and Ubox (where SGX keys were stored). A FW based solution was deployed to have SGX keys pulled from IO1 instead of IO0 to bypass this issue if I recall correctly. KPT solution was to not support KPT on IO0.

@Cummins, Michael K Thanks for your support on this issue debubg. Issue is not reproducible by applying S3M_ATT_DIS=1 fuse override. We are able to install the SGX PSW drivers and basic sgx_app test successful on WW47.3 CentOS release with BIOS 3727.D05. Fuse Override:  bt.go(compute_config ='x3', segment='CWFXDCC', pwrgooddelay=90, pwrgoodxml=r"C:\Intel\raritan.xml", pwrgoodmethod='manual', fused_unit=True, fuse_str_compute=['scf_gnr_maxi_coretile_c1_r5.core_fb_s3m_att_disable_fuse=0x1']) Note : SGX/TDX BIOS configuration goes for globalrest flow and which cleared the fuse override, so we followed below sequence to overcome the fuse override.                  1. Flash the IFWI and configure the SGX BIOS and rest the platform                  2. Make sure SGX enumeration successful.                  3. Override the Fuse : S3M_ATT_DIS=1           In this flow we are hitting an MCHECK error 0x4811(DEC_BLOB_FAILED_BAD_MAC_COMM_ERR), this error due to fuse override is happening after SGX configured which is not expected by MCHECK. To over come this we have additional WA. I.e  Enable SgxFactoryReset and do a fuse override.

Hi all, PV Security attempted this on SC09WVAW7495.amr.corp.intel.com This part has the SGX Fuse Correction for S3M_ATT_DIS=1 QDF: Q5VK Cores: 144C IFWI : BHSDCRB1.86B.3781.D03.2412021638_GB81000370_NA_SC830002f0_RB8a000020_CWFAP_1.bi DIMM: DDR5 RDIMM 96GB, 7200, 12 DIMMs Kernel: 6.8.0-cwf.bkc.6.8.8.2.9.x86_64 With this, we are able to install and run SGX AESM services without error. @Kumar K L, Sudhir , please upload the fuse dump and the passed logs.

Hangdumps Core and Uncore MCA dumps Status scope attached to Axon page
@Colton, Alexis A Could you please have a check on this UBOX and PUNIT MCA error found during sgx aesm service activation in CentOS 6.8 kernel
ISCLK errors are usually occurring only during reset. Was an error generated that sent you back through another reset? Also have we confirmed we have the SRF/GNR patch that deals with SGX keys on warm reset due to the IO die bug (that also impacts KPT keys)?
@Cummins, Michael K  We see system hungs ASAP we try to start the SGX aesm services at CentOS,(systemctl start sgx.aesm.serives). Can you point us what SRF/GNR SGX key issue you talking about.
Have you already addressed the other CWF SGX sighting: https://hsdes.intel.com/appstore/article/#/14023936962 The SRF/GNR issue that impacted SGX and KPT is from here: https://hsdes.intel.com/appstore/article/#/15013577215 The summary of the issue is that SGX and KPT keys were listed as pull once for IO0. However there is a power down that occurs after the initial fuse pull for QAT and Ubox (where SGX keys were stored). A FW based solution was deployed to have SGX keys pulled from IO1 instead of IO0 to bypass this issue if I recall correctly. KPT solution was to not support KPT on IO0.
@Cummins, Michael K Thanks for your support on this issue debubg. Issue is not reproducible by applying S3M_ATT_DIS=1 fuse override. We are able to install the SGX PSW drivers and basic sgx_app test successful on WW47.3 CentOS release with BIOS 3727.D05. Fuse Override:  bt.go(compute_config ='x3', segment='CWFXDCC', pwrgooddelay=90, pwrgoodxml=r"C:\Intel\raritan.xml", pwrgoodmethod='manual', fused_unit=True, fuse_str_compute=['scf_gnr_maxi_coretile_c1_r5.core_fb_s3m_att_disable_fuse=0x1']) Note : SGX/TDX BIOS configuration goes for globalrest flow and which cleared the fuse override, so we followed below sequence to overcome the fuse override.                  1. Flash the IFWI and configure the SGX BIOS and rest the platform                  2. Make sure SGX enumeration successful.                  3. Override the Fuse : S3M_ATT_DIS=1           In this flow we are hitting an MCHECK error 0x4811(DEC_BLOB_FAILED_BAD_MAC_COMM_ERR), this error due to fuse override is happening after SGX configured which is not expected by MCHECK. To over come this we have additional WA. I.e  Enable SgxFactoryReset and do a fuse override.

raw.comments:
++++14613335738 dbombien
Appears this may be a MCHECK error due to the population of the DIMMs on the platform. Please ensure the platform has the DIMMs populated in a configuration supporting SGX and TDX - requires uniform population across slots.

++++14613344100 gmuppala 
Issue reproducible on IFWI : BHSDCRB1.86B.3698.D03.2411041040 (WW45.1 PO purple release) We are hitting an UC MCA error while trying to start the sgx.aesm service on centos  #systemctl start sgx.aesm.services ************************************************************** System 1 : SC09WVAW7493.amr.corp.intel.com Board : Avenue City Stepping : 1S A0 Fuse : Q5VJ (fused) Bios ID         : BHSDCRB1.86B.3698.D03.2411041040 Kernel : 6.8.0-cwf.bkc.6.8.8.2.9.x86_64DIMM Config : 1DPC Micron RA64GB(16Gbx4DR)7200Freq  SGX DCAP      : SGX-2.24.100.3-v1-centos9 @Bombien, Derek  Platform is having 1DPC Micron RA64GB DIMMs, there is no MCHCEK error we could find on this failure. Hangdumps Core and Uncore MCA dumps Status scope attached to Axon page 


++++14613344645 gmuppala
@Colton, Alexis A Could you please have a check on this UBOX and PUNIT MCA error found during sgx aesm service activation in CentOS 6.8 kernel
++++1565922118 mkcummin
ISCLK errors are usually occurring only during reset. Was an error generated that sent you back through another reset? Also have we confirmed we have the SRF/GNR patch that deals with SGX keys on warm reset due to the IO die bug (that also impacts KPT keys)?
++++14613363877 gmuppala
@Cummins, Michael K  We see system hungs ASAP we try to start the SGX aesm services at CentOS,(systemctl start sgx.aesm.serives). Can you point us what SRF/GNR SGX key issue you talking about.

++++14613381738 mkcummin
Have you already addressed the other CWF SGX sighting: https://hsdes.intel.com/appstore/article/#/14023936962 The SRF/GNR issue that impacted SGX and KPT is from here: https://hsdes.intel.com/appstore/article/#/15013577215 The summary of the issue is that SGX and KPT keys were listed as pull once for IO0. However there is a power down that occurs after the initial fuse pull for QAT and Ubox (where SGX keys were stored). A FW based solution was deployed to have SGX keys pulled from IO1 instead of IO0 to bypass this issue if I recall correctly. KPT solution was to not support KPT on IO0.
++++1666289329 gmuppala 
@Cummins, Michael K Thanks for your support on this issue debubg. Issue is not reproducible by applying S3M_ATT_DIS=1 fuse override. We are able to install the SGX PSW drivers and basic sgx_app test successful on WW47.3 CentOS release with BIOS 3727.D05. Fuse Override:  bt.go(compute_config ='x3', segment='CWFXDCC', pwrgooddelay=90, pwrgoodxml=r"C:\Intel\raritan.xml", pwrgoodmethod='manual', fused_unit=True, fuse_str_compute=['scf_gnr_maxi_coretile_c1_r5.core_fb_s3m_att_disable_fuse=0x1']) Note : SGX/TDX BIOS configuration goes for globalrest flow and which cleared the fuse override, so we followed below sequence to overcome the fuse override.                  1. Flash the IFWI and configure the SGX BIOS and rest the platform                  2. Make sure SGX enumeration successful.                  3. Override the Fuse : S3M_ATT_DIS=1           In this flow we are hitting an MCHECK error 0x4811(DEC_BLOB_FAILED_BAD_MAC_COMM_ERR), this error due to fuse override is happening after SGX configured which is not expected by MCHECK. To over come this we have additional WA. I.e  Enable SgxFactoryReset and do a fuse override.


++++1666326722 mariatho
Hi all, PV Security attempted this on SC09WVAW7495.amr.corp.intel.com This part has the SGX Fuse Correction for S3M_ATT_DIS=1 QDF: Q5VK Cores: 144C IFWI : BHSDCRB1.86B.3781.D03.2412021638_GB81000370_NA_SC830002f0_RB8a000020_CWFAP_1.bi DIMM: DDR5 RDIMM 96GB, 7200, 12 DIMMs Kernel: 6.8.0-cwf.bkc.6.8.8.2.9.x86_64 With this, we are able to install and run SGX AESM services without error. @Kumar K L, Sudhir , please upload the fuse dump and the passed logs.

++++1666328569 skumarkl
Fuse Dump of the Syste SC09WVAW7495.amr.corp.intel.com fused part  QDF: Q5VK Cores: 144C IFWI : BHSDCRB1.86B.3781.D03.2412021638_GB81000370_NA_SC830002f0_RB8a000020_CWFAP_1.bin DIMM: DDR5 RDIMM 96GB, 7200, 12 DIMMs Kernel: 6.8.0-cwf.bkc.6.8.8.2.9.x86_64

WW43.3: MTC team able to connect to target SUT, Neil from ucode team is running some experiments get more understanding on failure cause
WW42.5 : MTC team facing challenges to get connected to target machine from MTC host using windbg, Sumant from MTC opened a ticket to unblock a debug port 
WW41.5: Debug continues from ucode team
WW40.5: Current understand is that the timeout is a slowness issue due to the RLPs taking too long to update the state and it leads to a reset, Debug still continues from uCode team
WW39.5: Trending like issue with the Fountaingrass ECO though, the RLPs are constantly in a loop gaining ownership of the monitor address, so maybe it takes a while for the RLP with matching APIC ID to make progress to wake up the all the RLPs
WW38.5 : Debug still continues from ucode team  
WW37.2:  this issue is isolated to an issue with Monitor\Mwait code in Windows.  The RLP failing to come out of MWAIT even when monitor address is getting written.  both Ucode and MTC team are looking into it.
WW35.5  MTC is still trying to enable network port to talk to SUT outside MTC lab
WW34.2  MTC team started the debug.  it sounds like they need some time to setup the right debug environment with symbol files
WW32.5 we need to get Windbg environment setup on debug SUT to make forward progress.  work in progress for setting up Windbg
WW30.5 Received another ucode patch.  also working with Windows team to setup windows debugger
WW29.4 received yet another patch from ucode team.  WIP to collect the hang dump
WW28.5 debug still continues with ucode team
WW27.5  the debug continues with ucode team.  hangdump was collected from the test patch and Suneil is looking into it
WW23.4;with the fountaingrass patch fix removed we see the system guard boots successfully.  
now Neil from fountaingrass TF involved in this debug to identify why fountaingrass fix causing this
WW21.3 Received an EB ACM from ACM team on WW21.3.  Verification pending
WW18.4.  Issue is consistent on all attempts.  GETSEC works clean.  the issue comes only when Wndows boots.  Going to get help from Windows team for next step

Seems a kernel issue: [313][T304]:tdx_vmm_dispatcher.c: tdx_vmm_dispatcher: 114: leaf_opcode = 0x2d [314][T304]:tdh_sys_config.c: check_tdmr_available_areas: 612: TDMR[3]: Non-reserved area [0xc000000000 - 0xe000000000] is not in any CMR [315][T304]:tdh_sys_config.c: tdh_sys_config: 841: Check and set TDMRs failed [316][T304]:tdx_vmm_dispatcher.c: tdx_vmm_post_dispatching: 1062: tdx_vmm_post_dispatching - preparing to do SEAMRET And according to the CMR info read from TDX module with TDH.SYS.RD, The CMR info is [  158.596677] virt/tdx: CMR[0]: [0x100000, 0x77800000) [  158.602357] virt/tdx: CMR[1]: [0x100000000, 0xbff4000000) [0xc000000000 - 0xe000000000] is not in any CMR range.
@Grams, Stanislaw the error is TDX_TDMR_OUTSIDE_CMRS

This issue is due to the host VMM pass the TDMR range [0xc000000000 - 0xe000000000] to TDX module but this range is not CMR. Fix it by add this range in reserved area. Have sent the fix patch to BKC team.

Correct myself. This issue can be fixed by adding the "modprobe.blacklist=kmem" in kernel cmdline. The root cause is the kmem driver host-add some CXL memory or NVDIMM before module initialization. It will result in failure to initialize the module as these hot-added memory are not in CMR but Linux kernel will config them in TDMR. This is expected in current TDX Linux design. To use TDX, it must disable kmem memory hotplug. I send the patch to add some pre-check so that it will return error info directly instead of triggering seamcall error.
@Qiang, Chenyi TDX initialization is working fine on TBOOT kernel by adding below arguments to kernel cmd line "modprobe.blacklist=kmem" kvm_intel.tdx=1" Pass logs

Hi all, This will be rejected, since this does not need a fix. The issue is caused due to incompatibility between CXL and TDX, which can be handled using a Work-around cmd as shown in the below comments.

The root cause is the kmem driver host-add some CXL memory or NVDIMM before module initialization. It will result in failure to initialize the module as these hot-added memory are not in CMR but Linux kernel will config them in TDMR. This is expected in current TDX Linux design. To use TDX, it must disable kmem memory hotplug. I send the patch to add some pre-check so that it will return error info directly instead of triggering seamcall error.

raw.bug.fix_description:
The root cause is the kmem driver host-add some CXL memory or NVDIMM before module initialization. It will result in failure to initialize the module as these hot-added memory are not in CMR but Linux kernel will config them in TDMR.

This is expected in current TDX Linux design. To use TDX, it must disable kmem memory hotplug.

This issue can be fixed by adding the "modprobe.blacklist=kmem kvm_intel.tdx=1" in kernel cmdline.

raw.server_platf.bug.root_cause_detail:
The root cause is the kmem driver host-add some CXL memory or NVDIMM before module initialization. It will result in failure to initialize the module as these hot-added memory are not in CMR but Linux kernel will config them in TDMR.

This is expected in current TDX Linux design. To use TDX, it must disable kmem memory hotplug.

This issue can be fixed by adding the "modprobe.blacklist=kmem kvm_intel.tdx=1" in kernel cmdline.
